// purpose: Debug Generator - the WEBVIEW project of apps/vscode-extension (AAP 0.7.3).
// two-projects: This workspace deliberately declares two composite projects, and this is the second of them. tsconfig.json is the extension HOST - a Node 24 process, `lib` ES2023 only, `types` ["node", "vscode"], which excludes src/webview/**. tsconfig.webview.json - THIS file - is the React application rendered inside the "Debug Generator" webview view, a browser document with no Node and no `vscode` module. The split is the mechanism, not a preference: one program cannot be honest about both environments at once. Keeping them apart is what makes a `window` reference in a host module a compile error and a `process.env` read in a webview module a compile error, which is the only guarantee either side gets - at runtime the webview is an iframe that has no Node globals, and the host has no document.
// program: src/webview/main.tsx mounts App.tsx, which composes QuestionForm, ProgressSteps, RelevantFiles, ModificationsList, DiffView, CaptureControls, AnalysisSummary, FollowUp, TargetBadge, PairingCode and StatusBar out of @debuggen/panel-renderer tokens and primitives (AAP 0.7.3), with src/webview/theme.ts mapping the `vscode-light`, `vscode-dark`, `vscode-high-contrast` and `vscode-high-contrast-light` body classes onto the light / dark / highContrast token themes (AAP 0.6.3) and src/webview/vscode-api.ts wrapping `acquireVsCodeApi()`.
// consumers: Four consumers read this one file and all four must stay satisfied. 1. `pnpm typecheck` at the root (`tsc -b` over the solution file) and this workspace's own `typecheck` script, which is `tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.webview.json` - both require `composite`. 2. `vite build` (`pnpm run build:webview`), which transpiles this same source set into dist/webview/main.js and dist/webview/main.css. Vite reads `jsx`, `target` and `lib` for its transform and never emits declarations, so the two must agree on the language level while only `tsc -b` type-checks. 3. typescript-eslint's project service, which resolves the type information behind the type-aware rules and eslint-plugin-react-hooks for src/webview/**/*.tsx - which is why the colocated tests are inside `include`: with the project service enabled a .ts(x) file that no project claims is a parsing error, not a lint finding. 4. the root vitest.config.ts project `vscode-extension-webview`, whose include glob is apps/vscode-extension/src/webview/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} under happy-dom. Every file that project collects is a member of this program, so `pnpm --filter debug-generator test` runs only code the gate has already type-checked.
// inherited: Everything not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, `moduleDetection: force`, the no-unused / no-implicit diagnostics and `target` ES2023. Nothing here relaxes a check: no `strict: false`, no `noImplicitAny: false`, no `allowJs`, no `skipDefaultLibCheck`. `noEmit` must never be added either - TypeScript 6.0.3 answers a referenced composite project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// format: Strict JSON, like the root tsconfig.json, tsconfig.base.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` read it, so no consumer - tsc, typescript-eslint's project service, Vitest, Vite or Prettier - has to know which one to reach for. The rationale therefore lives in the `"// …"` string keys of this object rather than in comments. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because this project is built by name (`tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.webview.json`) and referenced from the root solution file, and a non-composite project in either position fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate here. Vite does not read the option - it transpiles file by file - so its value serves the typecheck gate alone.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: "src" and not "." - the opposite of the host project, which spans src/**, test/** and vite.config.ts and therefore has to root at the workspace directory. This program spans exactly two input roots, src/webview/** and the single file src/webview-messages.ts (see `include`), whose common root is src/. Pinning it keeps the declaration mirror under .tsbuild/webview/ stable - src/webview/App.tsx -> .tsbuild/webview/webview/App.d.ts, src/webview-messages.ts -> .tsbuild/webview/webview-messages.d.ts - whereas leaving it unset would let the compiler infer the root from the longest common prefix of the inputs, which moves the whole tree whenever a file is added or removed. It also pins the program's boundary: a file outside src/ reached by `include` is rejected with TS6059 rather than silently emitting beside the sources. Note the interaction with the base's `tsBuildInfoFile`, which is overridden below for exactly this reason: with a nested `rootDir` TypeScript derives the default stamp location from `outDir` plus the path from `rootDir` back to the config file, which lands it outside this workspace.
// compilerOptions.declaration: `declaration`, `declarationMap` and `emitDeclarationOnly` are inherited true from the base and restated so the "declarations, never JavaScript" guarantee is local to this project: `composite` forbids `noEmit` (TS6310), so emitting nothing but .d.ts/.d.ts.map is the only shape that satisfies both the gate and Vite's ownership of dist/webview.
// compilerOptions.outDir: Declaration-only emit, restated with the `${configDir}` anchoring every sibling workspace uses. `${configDir}` resolves to the directory of THIS file, so both this path and the stamp below land in apps/vscode-extension/.tsbuild/webview - ignored by .gitignore, by .prettierignore and by the `**/.tsbuild/**` entry in eslint.config.js, so the gate never shows up in `git status`. What must never happen: tsc writing into apps/vscode-extension/dist. That directory belongs to esbuild.mjs (dist/extension.js, the manifest's `main`) and to `vite build` (dist/webview/main.js and dist/webview/main.css, which the webview view loads through its content-security-policy nonce) byte for byte, and `.vscodeignore` keeps dist/** inside the VSIX - so a stray .d.ts from the gate in there would be shipped inside the extension.
// compilerOptions.tsBuildInfoFile: THE SUBDIRECTORY IS LOAD-BEARING. tsconfig.base.json reserves this override for the second project in a directory, and apps/vscode-extension is the only workspace that has one: the host project keeps the base's .tsbuild/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo pair, and this project must move BOTH its output directory and its stamp underneath it. Two composite projects sharing one `outDir` overwrite each other's declarations, and two sharing one .tsbuildinfo never settle - every `tsc -b` run rebuilds both, with exit code 0 and no warning, which is the worst possible failure mode for a gate. The host project's `exclude` lists ".tsbuild" precisely so the declarations emitted here do not become inputs of its next run.
// compilerOptions.lib: Widened from the base's ES2023-only set, which exists so a Node-only package cannot reference `window` and still compile. This project is the opposite case and the ONLY place in this workspace where the browser libraries are legitimate: every module renders in a document. The webview legitimately uses `document`/`window` (theme.ts reads the `vscode-*` body classes and `window.matchMedia`, main.tsx mounts into a root element), `MessageEvent` and `window.addEventListener("message", ...)` for the host bridge in vscode-api.ts, `HTMLTextAreaElement`/`HTMLInputElement`/`KeyboardEvent` and `ClipboardEvent` behind QuestionForm, FollowUp and PairingCode, and `structuredClone`-free plain objects over `postMessage`. DOM.Iterable is what makes iteration over `NodeList`, `DOMTokenList` and `FormData` type-check. ES2023 is restated alongside the browser libs because `lib` REPLACES the inherited array rather than merging with it - omitting it here would silently drop `Array.prototype.findLast`, `toSorted`, `structuredClone`'s companions and the rest of the language level the rest of the monorepo is written against, and the resulting errors would point at call sites rather than at this line. No "WebWorker" (nothing here runs off the main thread) and no "DOM.AsyncIterable" (the webview consumes discrete messages, never a `ReadableStream`).
// compilerOptions.types: Empty, and empty ON PURPOSE - this is the environment boundary the host project's `types` array cannot express from the other side. The base sets no `types` at all, which means "include every @types package that is resolvable"; an empty array means "include none of them", so nothing is ambient in this program that a file did not import for itself. The three notes below are the concrete guarantees that buys.
// compilerOptions.types.node: @types/node 24.13.6 is a root devDependency and therefore resolvable from here, so without an empty `types` array `process.env.FOO`, `Buffer`, `__dirname`, `setImmediate` and `require` would all type-check inside a webview module and then throw in the iframe at runtime. With it they are errors at the only moment they can still be cheap.
// compilerOptions.types.vscode: @types/vscode 1.125.0 is a devDependency of this workspace and is the host project's most important entry. Keeping it out here means a bare `vscode.window.showTextDocument(...)` in a webview module is TS2304 ("Cannot find name 'vscode'") instead of compiling against an API the iframe does not have. Its exact limit, measured with tsc 6.0.3 rather than assumed: an EXPLICIT `import * as vscode from "vscode"` still type-checks, because module resolution finds node_modules/@types/vscode for that specifier no matter what `types` says, and the only compiler setting that could block it is a `paths` alias this repository forbids (see the `"// compilerOptions.not-set"` note below). That import is therefore caught elsewhere, and on purpose: `vite build` cannot resolve "vscode" into a browser bundle, the `no-restricted-imports` boundary for this workspace rejects it, and review treats it as a defect - because the webview talks to the host only through the typed union in src/webview-messages.ts, relayed by src/webview/vscode-api.ts over `acquireVsCodeApi()`.
// compilerOptions.types.mocha: @types/mocha is not wanted either. The Mocha globals belong to the extension-host suites under test/**, which are the host project's members; the suites collected here are Vitest suites and follow the repository-wide convention of importing their harness explicitly - `import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"` - so "vitest/globals" appears in no workspace of this monorepo. The `globals: true` setting on the `vscode-extension-webview` Vitest project exists for one runtime reason only: @testing-library/react 16.3.3 registers its automatic `cleanup` on the global `afterEach`. That is a runtime hook, not a type, so it needs nothing here.
// compilerOptions.types.imports-still-r: What an empty array does NOT block, which is why it costs this project nothing: explicitly imported types still resolve normally. React 19.3.0's types arrive through `import type { ReactNode } from "react"` and, for the automatic JSX runtime, through the compiler's own `react/jsx-runtime` module import; react-dom/client, @debuggen/panel-renderer, @debuggen/protocol and @debuggen/shared all resolve through their `exports` maps. Naming "react" or "react-dom" here would be wrong twice over - they are not ambient global type packages, and it would make their declarations program-wide instead of per-file.
// compilerOptions.jsx: NOT overridden: "jsx". The base's "react-jsx" (React 19.3.0 automatic runtime) is exactly right, so no .tsx file needs an `import React`. It must not become "react-jsxdev" here: this project is also what the production `vite build` type-checks against, and the dev runtime is Vite's own development-mode decision, not a committed compiler setting.
// compilerOptions.module: NOT overridden: "module" / "moduleResolution". The base's "ESNext" + "bundler" is the flavour AAP 0.3.4 assigns to extension and web code, and bundler resolution is a requirement rather than a taste here: it is what resolves @debuggen/panel-renderer's "." and "./styles.css" export conditions (a stylesheet subpath with no "types" condition, which NodeNext resolution treats far less kindly) and what lets Vite's own resolver and the compiler agree on every specifier.
// compilerOptions.module.specifiers: CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY FILE IN src/webview/**: relative specifiers are EXTENSIONLESS - `import { App } from "./App";` and `import type { HostToWebviewMessage } from "../webview-messages";` - as in the host half of this workspace and in packages/panel-renderer, and the exact opposite of the ".js"-suffixed convention that packages/shared, packages/protocol and packages/telemetry must use because they override this setting to NodeNext. An extensionless relative import that reports TS2835 ("did you mean './x.js'?") means this setting was overridden to NodeNext by accident, and the config is what gets fixed, never the imports.
// compilerOptions.module.stylesheets: STYLESHEET IMPORTS, the one resolution detail that needs a companion file: main.tsx imports "@debuggen/panel-renderer/styles.css" for the design system's tokens and base styles, and "./styles.css" for the webview's own sheet. Vite handles both, but TypeScript has no notion of a CSS module specifier, so each needs an ambient `declare module "*.css";` to type-check. The narrow, deliberate fix is a single ambient declaration file inside src/webview/ (for example src/webview/assets.d.ts, owned by the source author), which the "src/webview/**/*.ts" glob below already claims. It is NOT `allowJs`, NOT a widened `types` array and NOT a `paths` entry - each of those would buy the same result by loosening the whole program.
// compilerOptions.not-set: NOT set: "paths" / "baseUrl". The three workspace dependencies resolve through their `exports` maps plus the project references below, exactly as Vite and the runtime resolve them (AAP 0.2.2). An alias to a sibling's src/** would hide a broken `exports` map, let the webview import past a declared entry point and let the acyclic package layering be violated without anything failing. Because those maps point at each package's dist/index.d.ts, which lies outside the `${configDir}/.tsbuild` declaration directory, no output-to-source redirect applies to that target. Each package's `types` condition is therefore a fallback array, dist/ first and src/ second: a built tree resolves the dist/ declarations exactly as the bundlers ship them, while a tree with no dist/ yet (a fresh clone) resolves the source entry, which `tsc -b` redirects to that referenced project's own `.tsbuild` declarations. That is what lets `pnpm typecheck` stand alone without `pnpm build` (AAP 0.8.5), and tests/e2e/clean-clone.spec.ts proves it on a fresh copy of the tree.
// include: The webview program, in two parts. "src/webview/**/*.ts" and "src/webview/**/*.tsx" - the React application (main.tsx, App.tsx, the eleven components of AAP 0.7.3), theme.ts, vscode-api.ts, and the colocated *.test.tsx / *.test.ts suites. The tests are deliberately program members, exactly as in packages/panel-renderer: `tsc -b` is the typecheck gate, so `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` apply to them as they do to the sources, an untypechecked test is how contract drift escapes, and the same glob is what gives typescript-eslint's project service a program covering every linted file under src/webview/**. The ".ts" glob additionally claims any ambient asset declaration placed here (see the stylesheet note above). "src/webview-messages.ts" - the typed host<->webview message union, named as a literal path rather than by a glob so this project claims that one file and no other module from src/.
// include.webview-messages: THE OVERLAP ON src/webview-messages.ts IS INTENTIONAL AND MUST BE PRESERVED. The host project matches the same file with "src/**/*.ts" and does not exclude it, so both programs compile it. A relative import cannot cross a composite project boundary and both halves of the workspace import that module, so the overlap is the only way to type ONE message union for both sides. It is safe precisely because the module is environment-neutral and side-effect free - discriminated-union message shapes, their const vocabularies and the two pure parsers both endpoints validate every frame with, touching neither DOM nor Node globals; its only runtime imports are single-definition schemas of @debuggen/protocol and @debuggen/shared, and its top level does nothing but read properties of those schemas - and because the two projects emit into separate .tsbuild/ subdirectories (.tsbuild/src/webview-messages.d.ts for the host, .tsbuild/webview/webview-messages.d.ts here). Do not "fix" it by relocating the file, by duplicating the types (a second definition of a cross-boundary shape is the defect AAP 0.2.3 forbids) or by adding a third project to "own" it.
// include.pending-sources: A literal `include` path that does not exist yet contributes nothing to the program (only a `files` entry would error), which is why the entry is written here and not in `files`: this configuration stays correct while the workspace is built out. Until the first webview source lands, `tsc -b` on this project answers TS18003 ("No inputs were found in config file") - expected on an empty subtree, not a configuration fault.
// include.nothing-else: Nothing else belongs here: src/** outside src/webview/** is the host program, test/** holds the extension-host suites that need a real editor, esbuild.mjs and .vscode-test.mjs are plain Node ESM (linted, never compiled - `allowJs` stays false), vite.config.ts is a host-project member because it uses node:path/node:url, and media/** holds only the icons.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list rather than merging with it, so the output and vendored directories are named again here; every entry is resolved relative to this directory, meaning apps/vscode-extension/{dist,.tsbuild,node_modules,.vscode-test}. `include` above already restricts the inputs to src/, which leaves all four outside the program; these entries keep that true if `include` is ever widened, and ".tsbuild" in particular matters because TypeScript drops `outDir` from the input set automatically only when `exclude` is absent - without it this project's own emitted declarations would become inputs of its next run. "dist" belongs to esbuild.mjs and `vite build`; ".vscode-test" is where @vscode/test-electron unpacks a full VS Code build (or is symlinked to the shared cache) during `pnpm test:vscode`.
// exclude.scope: Note what `exclude` does NOT do: it filters the `include` globs only, so a file reached by an import still joins the program - `rootDir` above is what keeps inputs inside src/.
// references: Exactly three, foundational-first to match the root solution's ordering, and exactly the `@debuggen/*` edges the WEBVIEW half of this workspace has. ../../packages/shared - ids, `Result`, the error types and the single `SourceLocation` schema (AAP 0.2.3) that the relevant-files and modifications lists render and hand back to the host. ../../packages/protocol - `SessionRecord`, `AnalysisResult`, `InstrumentationPlan`-carrying messages and the progress payloads the view renders. They are consumed here for their types, for small pure helpers such as `assertNever`, and for the single-definition schemas (`sessionRecordSchema`, `analysisResultSchema`, `relevantFileSchema`, `sessionCleanupSchema`, `sourceLocationSchema`) that src/webview-messages.ts validates every host frame against - never for a transport: the webview never opens a socket, it exchanges the union in src/webview-messages.ts with the host, which owns the single connection to the local service (AAP 0.4.2). Zod therefore runs inside the webview bundle, and src/webview/csp-runtime.ts switches it to jitless mode before any schema is built, because the webview's content-security policy grants no 'unsafe-eval'. ../../packages/panel-renderer - the design system. This project is the only one in the workspace permitted to see it, and that permission is what lets the webview obey the zero-hardcoded-CSS rule of AAP 0.6.4 by importing tokens, layout and UI primitives instead of inventing styles. The host project deliberately omits it - host code has no page to render into.
// references.do-not-extend: Do not extend this list. apps/local-service is reached over HTTP and WebSocket and its contract is @debuggen/protocol; packages/telemetry, packages/panel-schema and packages/instrumentation arrive transitively as the types those two re-export, so a direct edge would only invert the layering; and apps/chrome-extension or apps/demo-app would additionally fail `pnpm check:no-hardcoding` (AAP 0.5.4).
// references.effect: What the references do, precisely: they order the build, so `tsc -b` on this project (or on the root solution) builds packages/shared, then packages/protocol - and, through protocol's and the renderer's own references, packages/telemetry, packages/instrumentation and packages/panel-schema - before this project, and reports errors in dependency order. They are not what resolves the three specifiers; the `exports` maps are, per the `"// compilerOptions.not-set"` note above.
